It's something that always bothered me about reddit. Negative karma is what keeps you from voicing your opinion and motivates you to have the same opinion as the majority. If you mean an exodus from Facebook to Voat, I don't think it would translate well.

Facebook is more of a family/friend-based social media for sharing content with people who you know intimately. On there you can share pictures of yourself that only your friends can see and chat directly with people who you explicitly know.

Voat on the other hand cloaks individuals behind their pseudonyms and content is available for all to vote on.

But if you mean from Facebook to a new social media website, the newbie would have to somehow outdo the giant that is Facebook. Granted there are better newer sites available, but Facebook has spread itself to being useful outside its own website. One of its greatest features is that you can use your Facebook account for logging in on other websites and all the integrated like-buttons that are present on many popular websites. A new website would have to offer this and more if it were to try and take FB's current users.

I meant the latter, but more in terms of people being fed up with facebook's bullshit than a competitor poaching users. Although it would obviously be a combination of both factors for it to ever actually happen.
